description: Name the vendor and get their official tool, paste-ready config and a fallback in one call, faster than a web search to a working setup, and an honest 'nothing fits' when that's the truth. Call this after a failed setup, under constraints (no account, nothing paid, no new key, headless, self-hosted), for a niche job, and before telling the user something can't be done. Pass the job in plain words; one call returns one decisive best_pick (why it fits the constraints, exact setup steps in best_pick.setup / use_it, a fallback) or an honest abstain (verdict nothing_good_found / cannot_work_as_asked / not_a_tool_job / too_broad, with answer and, for not_a_tool_job or too_broad, curated workaround steps). Evidence age is shown prominently as last-checked DATE — never a stale 'live' claim. best_pick.summary is the one line to show a human; report_call is the follow-up after you use it. Constraints written in the job or in constraints are checked per result. Free, no key. Returns a top-level report_token for optional feedback.

healthy_only.description: only entries whose latest check passed: MCP handshake ok or auth_required, or (HTTP APIs) base URL reachable

no_admin.description: no admin install or third-party approval

no_new_key.description: no new API key, token or scopes

read_only.description: only entries whose every server is verified read-only

require.description: same constraints as a list, e.g. ["no_account","no_paid"]; constraints written in the job text are also read

detail.description: brief drops per-result score_breakdown and why[] (about 4x smaller); default full

job.description: The task in plain words, e.g. 'send SMS to customers', 'read my Google Calendar', 'GitHub MCP server'

watcher_key.description: optional: get an alert if nothing good is found now but a match appears later

name: search_tools
